key_insight: Hybrid Reasoning Agents combine internal latent reasoning with external text-based interaction, letting an agent think efficiently in a hidden space while still using language to communicate and act. This bridges the gap between fast private reasoning and transparent, tool-using behavior.
problem_solved: Current LLM agents mostly reason and interact through text, which can be slower and less efficient than latent reasoning. Pure latent reasoning is efficient but struggles with tool access, external actions, and interpretability; this paper addresses that tradeoff.
method: Uses a unified generation process that dynamically switches between latent reasoning and text-based outputs.
Allows the agent to keep reasoning internally while exposing text only when needed for communication or tool use.
Aims to preserve the efficiency of latent computation without losing the practicality and transparency of language-driven agents.
impact: This approach could make AI agents more efficient, flexible, and capable in real-world tasks that require both deep internal reasoning and external interaction. For practitioners, it offers a new design pattern for building agents that are faster than pure text-only systems yet still usable in existing tool ecosystems.
